hints: Look at what the two tests are really telling you, one test changes the mass in a very predictable way and the other tells you about a specific group next to the carbonyl.
Remember that $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces a ketone to a secondary alcohol by adding two H atoms, so a mass gain of 2 corresponds to a 2.3256% increase.

Once you have the molecular formula for a $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}\text{O}$ ketone, combine it with the need for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group and count how many different non-cyclic alkyl groups can complete the molecule.
walkthrough:
**Use the reduction mass gain to find Mr**

Think simply first. $\text{NaBH}_4$ turns $\text{C=O}$ into $\text{CH-OH}$. That is a gain of two hydrogen atoms.

So the mass increase is exactly 2:
$$\text{increase in } M_r = 2$$
$$\frac{2}{M_r(\text{X})} \times 100 = 2.3256$$

**Calculate Mr and the molecular formula**

Rearranging gives a lovely whole number. This is a good sign you are on track.

$$M_r(\text{X}) = \frac{2 \times 100}{2.3256} = 86.0$$
For a saturated, non-cyclic ketone with one $\text{C=O}$, the general formula is $\text{C}_n\text{H}_{2n}\text{O}$:
$$14n + 16 = 86$$
$$14n = 70, \text{ so } n = 5$$
So X is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

**Use the iodoform test to fix part of the structure**

A yellow precipitate with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ is the triiodomethane (iodoform) test. For a ketone, this is positive only for a methyl ketone.

X must contain:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$$
So X must be of the form $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-\text{R}$ where R is a $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7$ alkyl group.

**Count the isomeric ketones**

Now it is just an isomer counting job. How many different $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7$ groups can attach to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ while keeping the molecule non-cyclic?

There are only two: $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{-CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$.

That gives pentan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, and 3-methylbutan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. So there are 2 possibilities.

options.A: Incorrect. Choosing 1 usually means you found pentan-2-one but missed the branched isomer 3-methylbutan-2-one. Both contain the required $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group and have formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.
options.B: Correct. $M_r = 86$ gives $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, and the positive iodoform test requires $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. Only two non-cyclic ketones fit: pentan-2-one and 3-methylbutan-2-one.
options.C: Incorrect. There are not three methyl ketones of formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Students sometimes wrongly count pentan-3-one, but $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group so it is iodoform negative.
options.D: Incorrect. There are not four isomers. This error often comes from counting all $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ ketones including pentan-3-one and 3-methylbutan-2-one variants, or from including aldehydes or cyclic isomers, which are excluded by the question.
